question: The world's rivers deliver about 37,000 km³ of fresh water to the sea each year. How many million cubic metres is that per second?
answer: 37 million million / 31.5 million ≈ 1.2 million m³ per second.
move: Put a river and a sea current in one unit before comparing them.
trap: Losing a factor of a thousand when turning km³ into m³.
hint: Turn cubic kilometres into cubic metres, and a year into seconds.
steps: 37,000 km³ is 37,000 × 1,000,000,000 m³, or 37 million million m³.
A year has about 31.5 million seconds.
37 million million / 31.5 million ≈ 1.2 million m³ per second.
simply: Oceanographers call a million cubic metres a second one sverdrup. Every river on Earth together makes about one; the Antarctic Circumpolar Current alone carries well over a hundred.
reference: Dai & Trenberth, Estimates of freshwater discharge from continents: latitudinal and seasonal variations, Journal of Hydrometeorology, 2002
